# CSS fixtures of the visual matrix

The matrix in `test/tests/css/matrix.js` runs the same scenarios (form, list, modal, indicator, error,
offline) against five styles: Tailwind CSS v4, Bootstrap 5, Bulma 1, Pico CSS 2 and plain CSS. The sheets
are files of this repository, served by the test runner. **Nothing is fetched from a CDN when the tests
run.**

## Third-party files

All four are MIT licensed. Each one sits next to the license file of its project, and the licenses gate
(`ypy ci licenses`) checks that the license is recognised and on the allowlist.

|---|---|---|---|---|

The project has no Node dependency: the files were downloaded once (`curl` and `tar` on the registry
tarballs) and are kept here. To update one, download the new version, replace the file and its row, and
run `go test ./internal/styling`.

## Tailwind

`tailwind/tailwind.css` is the output of Tailwind for the classes of `tailwind/fixture.js` (the page markup
of the matrix) and the variants of `src/css/ypy-tailwind.css`. It was built with the standalone CLI
(a single executable, no Node), version 4.3.5, from this directory:

```sh
tailwindcss -i tailwind/input.css -o tailwind/tailwind.css
```

`tailwind/input.css` is the whole configuration: `@import "tailwindcss"`, the YPY variants, and
`@source "./fixture.js"`. The output is committed, so the tests need no Tailwind. After a change to
`fixture.js` or to the variants, build it again; `go test ./internal/styling` fails when a class of the
fixture is missing from the sheet.

## Files written for the matrix

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `*/fixture.js` | the markup of each scenario for one style, and what its page script does (open a modal) |
| `bootstrap/site.css`, `bulma/site.css`, `pico/site.css` | what a site of that framework writes to style the YPY states with the `data-ypy-state` attribute and the framework's own custom properties |
| `plain/plain.css` | the whole style of the plain-CSS case |
| `lib.js` | helpers of the tests (load a sheet, read layout and computed style) |

The tests check layout and computed style (box positions, colours, `display`, `opacity`). The runner
does not capture screenshots.
